scenes.title: Happiness, the Target
scenes.summary: Every person and every city aims at happiness and its parts in what they choose and avoid; so all exhortation and dissuasion concern what produces it or hinders it.

scenes.title: What Happiness Is
scenes.summary: Happiness is doing well with virtue, or self-sufficiency of life, or the pleasantest life with security, or abundance of possessions and bodies with the power to keep and use them. Its parts are good birth, friends, wealth, children, a good old age, the excellences of the body, reputation, honor, good fortune and virtue, goods of the soul and body within and of fortune without.

scenes.title: Good Birth and Good Children
scenes.summary: Good birth for a city is to be sprung from the soil or ancient, with distinguished founders; for a family, legitimacy and notable ancestors. Good children means a numerous, strong and self-controlled youth, and daughters of beauty and industry; a people whose women are bad, like the Lacedaemonians, is almost half unhappy.

scenes.title: Wealth
scenes.summary: The parts of wealth are coin, land, estates, furniture, slaves and livestock, secure, fit for a free man and useful; possessions are secure when their use is in one's power, one's own when one can give or sell them. Being rich lies in using rather than owning.

scenes.title: Reputation and Honor
scenes.summary: Good reputation is to be thought a person of worth; honor is a sign of a reputation for doing good, given for benefits that are hard to come by. Its parts are sacrifices, memorials, privileges, front seats, tombs, statues, public maintenance, barbarian prostrations, and gifts, which please lovers of money and of honor alike.

scenes.title: The Body and Old Age
scenes.summary: Health of a kind that lets a man use his body, unlike Herodicus' regimen; beauty, different for the young, the man in his prime and the old; strength, stature, and the athlete's excellence in running, wrestling, boxing, the pancration and the pentathlon; and a good old age, slow and painless, which needs fortune as well.

scenes.title: Friends and Fortune
scenes.summary: A friend is one who does for another's sake what he thinks good for him. Good fortune is the coming of the goods fortune causes, the envied goods of nature and the unexpected ones: the one handsome brother, the treasure found, the arrow that missed. Virtue is left for the discussion of praise.
